The Section on Detailed Exposition (Paṭiniddesavāra) – Analysis 16
The Analysis of the Mode of Conveying Coordination.
Therein, what is the mode of conveying coordination?
It is that which states: "Those phenomena which have a certain root, and those which are shown by the Sage to have the same meaning."
In a single footing, as many footings as descend [into it] must all be superimposed.
This is because, as in the case of the Mode of Conveying a Conversion, many footings descend [into it].
Therein, the superimposition is fourfold: the footing, the synonym, the development, and the abandoning.
In this context, what is the application by way of the proximate cause?
“To refrain from all evil,
to cultivate the wholesome;”
“The purification of one’s own mind—
this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
What is its proximate cause?
The three types of good conduct—
good conduct of body, good conduct of speech, and good conduct of mind—
this is the proximate cause.
Therein, that which is good conduct of body and speech is the aggregate of virtue (sīlakkhandha).
Within good conduct of mind, non-covetousness and non-ill will are the aggregate of concentration (samādhikkhandha).
Right view is the aggregate of wisdom (paññākkhandha).
This is the proximate cause: therein, the aggregate of virtue and the aggregate of concentration are serenity; the aggregate of wisdom is insight. This is the proximate cause:
therein, the fruit of serenity is the liberation of mind through the fading away of lust; the fruit of insight is the liberation by wisdom through the fading away of ignorance.
This is the proximate cause.
The forest is the footing for the jungle.
What is the forest?
And what is the jungle?
“Forest” (vana) refers to the five strands of sensual pleasure; craving is the thicket (vanatha).
This is the proximate cause (padaṭṭhāna).
“Forest” also refers to the grasping of signs, such as “woman” or “man.”

“Forest” (*vana*) refers to the grasping of the secondary characteristics of various limbs and members, thinking: “Oh, what an eye! Oh, what an ear! Oh, what a nose! Oh, what a tongue! Oh, what a body!
This is the proximate cause.
“Forest” also refers to the six internal and external sense bases when they are not fully understood.
The fetter that arises dependent upon both of these is the "thicket" (*vanatha*).
This is its proximate cause (*padaṭṭhāna*).
What is called the "thicket" is the underlying tendency (*anusaya*).
“Vanatha” means obsession (*pariyuṭṭhāna*).
This is the proximate cause (*padaṭṭhāna*).
Therefore the Blessed One said: “Having cut through both the forest and the thicket.”
This is the application by way of the proximate cause.
In this context, what is the application by way of synonyms?
The fading away of lust is the liberation of mind that is the fruit of training.
Through the fading away of ignorance, there is liberation by wisdom, which is the fruit of one beyond training.
This is a synonym.
Through the fading away of lust, there is liberation of mind, which is the fruit of non-returning.
Through the fading away of ignorance, there is liberation by wisdom, which is the supreme fruit, namely, Arahantship.
This is a synonym.
Through the fading away of lust, there is liberation of mind, which is the transcending of the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu).
Through the fading away of ignorance, there is liberation by wisdom and the transcendence of the three realms.
This is a synonym.
[It is also] the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the training in higher wisdom, the aggregate of wisdom, and the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment.
The enlightenment factor of equanimity, knowledge, right view, investigation, thorough investigation, moral shame, insight,
knowledge of phenomena— all this is a synonym.
This is the coordination by means of synonyms.
In this context, what is the application through development?
As the Blessed One said: “Therefore, bhikkhu, dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
Here, “ardent” refers to the faculty of energy (*vīriyindriya*).
"Clearly comprehending" refers to the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*).
"Mindful" refers to the faculty of mindfulness (*satindriya*).
"Having removed covetousness and dejection regarding the world" refers to the faculty of concentration (*samādhindriya*).
For one who dwells thus contemplating the body as a body, the four foundations of mindfulness reach fulfillment by development.
For what reason?
Because the four faculties have a single characteristic.
When the four foundations of mindfulness are being developed, the four right endeavors reach fulfillment through development.
When the four right endeavors are being developed, the four bases for psychic power reach fulfillment through development.
When the four bases for psychic power are being developed, the five faculties reach fulfillment through development.
Thus all [the factors] are so.
For what reason?

Because all the states conducive to enlightenment are factors of enlightenment; they have a single characteristic by virtue of the characteristic of leading out. Due to having this single characteristic, they reach the fulfillment of development.
This is the application by way of development.
In this regard, what is the application by way of abandoning?
One who dwells contemplating the body in the body abandons the perversion that "there is beauty in the ugly," and his [craving for] physical food...

Food comes to be fully understood; one becomes non-clinging through clinging to sensual pleasures, detached from the bond of sensual pleasure, dissociated from the bodily tie of covetousness, free from the taint of sensual pleasure, crossed over the flood of sensual pleasure, and without the barb of lust.
Furthermore, his station of consciousness based on form comes to be fully understood.
He proceeds; his lust for the form realm has been abandoned, and he does not proceed by way of bias due to desire.
Dwelling contemplating feelings in feelings, he abandons the perversion that "there is pleasure in what is suffering.
Contact as his nutriment comes to be fully understood, and he becomes non-clinging through the clinging to existence, and is dissociated from the fetter of existence.
He becomes dissociated from the bodily tie of ill will; he becomes free from the taint of existence;
he has crossed over the flood of existence; he becomes free from the dart of hatred; his station of consciousness dependent on feeling reaches full understanding;
his lust for the element of feeling is abandoned; and he does not go to a state of aversion.
Dwelling contemplating mind as mind, one abandons the perversion of perceiving the impermanent as permanent;
one brings the nutriment of consciousness to full understanding; one becomes non-clinging through the clinging to views; one becomes dissociated from the bond of views;
one becomes disjoined from the bodily tie of adherence to rules and observances; and one becomes taintless through the taint of views.

He has crossed over the flood of views, he is free from the barb of the mind, his station of consciousness based on perception comes to full understanding, his lust for the element of perception is abandoned, and he does not go toward a state of fear.
Dwelling contemplating phenomena as phenomena, he abandons the perversion of "self in what is non-self"; [this applies to] mental volition.
His nutriment comes to full understanding; he becomes non-clinging through the clinging to a self-theory;
he becomes dissociated from the bond of ignorance; he becomes detached from the bodily tie of adherence to "this is the truth";
he becomes taintless through the taint of ignorance; he has crossed over the flood of ignorance; and he becomes free from the barb of delusion.
His station of consciousness, which takes conditioned phenomena as its form, comes to be fully understood;
his lust for the element of formations is abandoned, and he does not go to a state of delusion.
This is the application by means of abandoning.
Therefore the Venerable Mahākaccāyana said:
“Those phenomena which have a certain root,
and those which are explained by the Sage as having a single meaning;”
"They are to be superimposed;
this is the Mode of Conveying Superimposition.
The Mode of Conveying Superimposition is concluded.
The analysis of the necklaces is finished.
